readers.summary: The decision round is a 3-round concurrent pipeline (run_decision_pipeline, engine/decision_phase.py) issuing up to ~12 LLM calls per committed decision: interpretation + up-to-3 actor roleplays (round 1), pushback + 5 omissions scans + quality assessment (round 2), then 1-4 advisor reactions + 1 summary fold (round 3). The house output format is deliberately NOT JSON: labelled plain-text lines ('QUALITY: poor', 'TRUST_CHANGE: -8') read by a shared tolerant parser (llm/parsing.py) with per-field defaults, parse-health telemetry, and a deterministic fallback per family — the one YAML call is inject generation. Three calls already return machine-read numbers/enums that MUTATE state (quality assessment's metric deltas + multiplier, actor TRUST_CHANGE/WILL_SUPPORT, diplomacy OUTCOME/ALLIANCE_COHESION_DELTA), so an authoritative spatial layer would extend an established, battle-tested pattern rather than invent one. The adjudicating calls currently see NO force positions at all: the quality assessment sees only narrative_state.to_llm_context() (metrics, synopsis, ledger, trust), and only the interpretation call sees uk_forces — as a raw str(dict) — and its already-prompted structured labels (FORCES INVOLVED / RESOURCES CONSUMED / TIMELINE) are returned verbatim and never parsed (game_manager returns 'forces_involved': [] as an explicit placeholder). The cheapest honest build: (a) a typed unit-position table (new WorldState field; leave dead spatial_state alone) rendered as ~20-50 lines (~450-1300 tokens) into the fast-moving tail of the shared context, (b) movement orders emitted either as a new section of the quality-assessment reply (zero extra latency, but raises its 400-token cap and overloads the effects-deciding call) or as a third task appended to round 3 (zero extra wall-clock — round 3 has 2 tasks against MAX_ROUND_WORKERS=3 — richest inputs, clean no-movement fallback, but shifts master-RNG draw count and thus cross-version replays), (c) red-force movement entering through the inject YAML (add optional movements: list, parsed in the tolerant apply_inject_effects style) and/or an optional FORCE_POSTURE label on the RUS actor reply. Actor simulation can consume spatial facts via to_actor_context — but needs a per-capital visibility filter mirroring get_diplomatic_context's fail-closed rule (ER-014/ER-018).
facts: CALL INVENTORY, round 1 (engine/decision_phase.py:355-402): (1) interpretation - interpret_player_action (agents/conversation.py:330-360), LLMContext.DECISION_INTERPRETATION, FLASH tier (llm/model_config.py:36). Input: build_shared_context_prefix (transcript dossier up to 60k chars, llm/context_builder.py:366-454) + str(dict) of uk_forces (4,103 chars), stockpiles (814 chars), constraints + action, via hot-editable template data/prompts/decision_interpretation.txt. Prompt REQUESTS labels INTERPRETATION/FORCES INVOLVED/RESOURCES CONSUMED/TIMELINE/FEASIBILITY but the reply is returned as ONE unparsed string; empty reply only records a parse-health fallback (conversation.py:358-360); task exception falls back to the raw action text (decision_phase.py:379,387). GameManager.interpret_decision returns 'forces_involved': [] and 'timeline': 'Immediate' as literal placeholders (engine/game_manager.py:423-424).

(2) actor_simulation - simulate_actor_responses (engine/actor_simulation.py:119-158), LLMContext.ACTOR_SIMULATION, PRO tier; up to 3 prompts fanned out via generate_group/batch_generate_text. Input per actor: identity + hidden state (motivations, agendas, redlines, capabilities) + narrative_state.to_actor_context() + per-actor Mystery narrative + action (actor_simulation.py:27-98). Output: labelled PUBLIC_RESPONSE/PRIVATE_ASSESSMENT/TRUST_CHANGE/WILL_SUPPORT/CONDITIONS/INTEL_SHARED; parsed by _parse_actor_response (161-333) with tolerant labels, next-line pending values, continuation accumulation, residue recording; per-field defaults (trust 0, will_support 'conditional'); empty/'[ERROR:' slot or parse exception -> _heuristic_actor_response (335-345).

CALL INVENTORY, round 2 (decision_phase.py:404-436): (3) pushback - generate_advisor_pushback (conversation.py:363-452), ADVISOR_PUSHBACK, FLASH, 1 call. Output: 'Role: concern' lines gated by a known-role whitelist (conversation.py:404-434) plus standalone 'NO PUSHBACK' sentinel; orphan lines recorded as misses, empty messages dropped; failure -> []. (4) critical_omissions - check_critical_omissions (conversation.py:455-619), CRITICAL_OMISSIONS, PRO, 5 calls (one per advisor, batched). Output: CONCERN/RECOMMENDATION labels or NO_CONCERN sentinel; concern-without-recommendation gets a placeholder, recommendation-without-concern is dropped; failure -> advisor silently skipped. (5) quality_assessment - assess_action_quality (engine/narrative_adjudication.py:177-257), QUALITY_ASSESSMENT, PRO, max_tokens=400. Input: narrative_state.to_llm_context() + action + interpretation. Output: QUALITY enum(exceptional/good/adequate/poor/catastrophic), REASONING (shown to player VERBATIM - the call is player-facing and never receives the Mystery narrative), EFFECTS: three named metric deltas, QUALITY MULTIPLIER (clamped 0.5-2.5). Parsed by _parse_quality_response (331-509); metric lines only accepted for the three whitelisted names (391-403); missing quality defaults 'adequate' with record_miss; exception -> _heuristic_quality_assessment (260-328).

CALL INVENTORY, round 3 (decision_phase.py:487-513): (6) character_responses - generate_character_responses (narrative_adjudication.py:606-668), CHARACTER_RESPONSE, FLASH, 1-4 prompts (NSA always, others by effect magnitude, 671-694), max_tokens=300; free prose, no parse; empty/'[ERROR:' -> '[Name] Understood, Prime Minister.' (7) situation_summary - compute_situation_summary (narrative_adjudication.py:796-874), SITUATION_SUMMARY, PRO, max_tokens=400; free prose fold with explicit fidelity rules; empty/exception -> deterministic fallback_situation_summary (908-941). So a full commit = up to 12 LLM calls; with a preview (ER-074, game_manager.py:529-532, decision_phase.py:371-434) interpretation+pushback+omissions are reused as no-LLM lambdas whose child seeds are STILL drawn, so only actor sim + quality + round 3 hit the model.

STATE MUTATION FROM PARSED LLM NUMBERS (proves the trust precedent): no-actor path scales the quality assessment's own suggested_effects by its own multiplier (clamped +/-20) and writes them onto narrative_state.hidden_metrics (decision_phase.py:465-481); actor path blends 60% calculate_effects_from_responses (derived from parsed WILL_SUPPORT enums and TRUST_CHANGE ints weighted by diplomatic_influence, actor_simulation.py:400-460) with 40% quality effects, in a FIXED metric order to keep dict order deterministic (_METRIC_ORDER, decision_phase.py:96, 455-463). resolve_decision then copies hidden_metrics over world.metrics (game_manager.py:568-573) - the documented one-way sync trap.

OTHER STRUCTURED CALLS: diplomacy outcome assessor parses OUTCOME enum(SUCCESS/NEUTRAL/FAILURE) + ALLIANCE_COHESION_DELTA signed int + SUMMARY (engine/diplomacy.py:288-460) and applies the delta to world.metrics. Inject generation is the ONLY YAML call: prompt demands a ```yaml block with id/title/description/channel/effects[{metric, delta}] (llm/prompts.py:458-470); parsed by yaml.safe_load with unclosed-fence tolerance and title/description schema check (llm/inject_generator.py:85-137); failure -> None -> diegetic quiet-turn inject (engine/sim_loop.py:38-55,393-399). Effect deltas tolerate int/float/quoted/annotated/'min..max' range shapes (sim_loop.py:229-267); unknown metric/unreadable delta -> skipped WITH a visible transcript line and record_miss - the exact template for how unknown unit/location ids in a movements list should fail.

PARSING INFRASTRUCTURE the movement schema would reuse: llm/parsing.py (143 lines) - extract_label (decoration-tolerant 'LABEL:' reader), find_signed_int/find_float (search, not convert), match_enum (exact -> worded-refusal -> unnegated-token, with negation lookback), is_sentinel_line, strip_decoration. llm/parse_health.py - record_miss/record_fallback/record_truncation/record_residue registry; router converts provider finish_reason 'length'/'MAX_TOKENS' into truncation events automatically (llm/router.py:123-137). Router retries each call once then substitutes MockDeterministicDriver output, never raising (router.py:380-393); batch drivers mark per-slot failure as '[ERROR: ...]' text that every consumer must (and does) guard.

WORLD-STATE CONTEXT THE ADJUDICATOR SEES TODAY: quality assessment (the effects-deciding call) sees ONLY narrative_state.to_llm_context() (models/narrative_state.py:311-350): raw hidden metric numbers with bands, situation_summary, last-3 recent_events, active_crises, the DECISIONS AND OUTCOMES ledger (~94 chars/turn), character trust lines. NO forces, NO stockpiles, NO locations, NO transcript. Actor sim sees the same minus trust (to_actor_context, ER-014). Interpretation/pushback/omissions see the shared dossier (whole-turn transcript window <=60k chars ~15k tokens + current metrics + ledger, context_builder.py:42,366-454) but only interpretation sees uk_forces. Inject generation sees metrics + synopsis + ledger + last-turn slice - no ORBAT. get_adjudicator_context (context_builder.py:651-697) is a ready-made adjudication context builder with ZERO callers - dead scaffolding at exactly this seam.

TOKEN COST OF A POSITION BLOCK: a one-line-per-unit table ('HMS_Prince_of_Wales | carrier | Portsmouth | not_highest_readiness | 8 F-35 embarked' ~80-110 chars ~20-27 tokens). 20 lines + header ~450-550 tokens; 50 lines ~1,100-1,350 tokens. Against current prompt sizes: quality assessment's whole context is ~350-700 tokens (to_llm_context) so the block roughly doubles the SMALLEST deciding prompt yet stays absolutely tiny; the transcript-carrying prompts run to ~15k tokens, so the block is <4-8% there. Added to the 5 deciding calls (interpretation + 3 actors + quality) it costs ~2.5-6.5k input tokens/turn; added to all ~12 calls ~6-16k/turn. Scenario ground truth: 18 typed UK units (9 naval, 9 air) with id/type/location/status/readiness fields already in data/scenarios/war_game_2025/initial_conditions.yaml; red_forces is aggregate counts (15 subs) with a single location 'North_Atlantic_rendezvous' + heading; a 3-group locations gazetteer (uk 8, operational_areas 3, russia 1) exists in the same file - the ~30-entry gazetteer of the prior study.

WorldState.spatial_state (models/world.py:40-43) confirmed written nowhere and read nowhere in *.py outside an audit SVG; WorldState is fully serialised via world.dict() in GameManager.to_dict (game_manager.py:836), so a NEW typed field (e.g. unit_positions: Dict[str, UnitPosition]) rides saves for free, and old saves load clean via default_factory - the same versioning trick PlayedEvent's ER-077 fields used (narrative_state.py:67-73).

DETERMINISM CONTRACT (the thing not to break): run_round pre-draws one child seed per task from the master rng IN TASK-LIST ORDER before dispatch (decision_phase.py:151-194); the documented fixed order is round1: interpretation, actor_simulation; round2: pushback, critical_omissions, quality_assessment; round3: character_responses, situation_summary (docstring 327-337). Skipped/preview-reused tasks stay in the list as no-LLM lambdas precisely so seed draws never shift. tests/test_decision_phase.py locks byte-identical replay at fixed seed and preview-vs-full seed stability; tests/test_prompt_cache_order.py locks the dossier ordering (transcript before per-turn state, ledger after transcript).

MOCK DRIVER COUPLING: llm/mock_driver.py selects canned variants by zlib.crc32 over prompt text (_stable_index, mock_driver.py:20-24) and detects call families by exact persona/format lines ('ACTION QUALITY:', 'You are the {role}...', the PUBLIC_RESPONSE format block). Any prompt text change reshuffles which canned variant every mock campaign gets, and a new MOVEMENT section has no mock counterpart - mock/offline campaigns would return no movement unless the mock grows a handler.
insertion_points: A. Inside the quality-assessment reply (extend the QUALITY/REASONING/EFFECTS format in assess_action_quality, narrative_adjudication.py:211-249, with e.g. 'MOVEMENT ORDERS:' lines 'unit_id: current_location -> destination | status', parsed by extending _parse_quality_response in its established label/pending/residue style). Latency: zero new rounds - it already runs concurrently in round 2 on PRO tier. Fragility: HIGH-MEDIUM. Requires adding the unit table to a prompt that today sees no ORBAT (small - it is the smallest prompt); requires raising max_tokens=400 to ~700 or the trailing EFFECTS/MULTIPLIER fields get truncated first (router records the truncation but the metric deltas are lost - a regression in the game's core loop); overloads the one call whose REASONING is shown to the player verbatim and whose verdict scales all effects, so a model that spends its budget on movement degrades the adjudication itself. Fallback is naturally safe: heuristic assessment carries no movement -> positions persist unchanged.

B. New third task appended to round 3 (add ('movement_adjudication', run, lambda: []) to the round3 list in run_decision_pipeline decision_phase.py:492-505 and mirrored in _run_reactions_and_summary_round narrative_adjudication.py:944-979 for the CLI path). Latency: zero wall-clock - round 3 currently holds 2 tasks against MAX_ROUND_WORKERS=3 (decision_phase.py:91), so the third slot is free; it is also the richest input point: action, interpretation, quality verdict, applied final_effects and parsed actor responses are all in hand. Fragility: LOW per-call (a small dedicated prompt: unit table + action + adjudicated outcome -> only MOVE lines; new LLMContext.MOVEMENT family gives it its own model tier, parse-health bucket and call-log identity for ~10 lines in model_config.py). Costs: one extra PRO/FLASH call per turn; APPEND-ONLY placement keeps existing tasks' child seeds intact within a run, but the master rng draws 3 seeds instead of 2 for round 3, so same-seed replays across code versions diverge from that round on (in-version determinism and saved-RNG-state resumes are unaffected - saves carry rng_state, game_manager.py:860).

C. Piggyback on the interpretation call (it ALREADY asks for FORCES INVOLVED / RESOURCES CONSUMED / TIMELINE in data/prompts/decision_interpretation.txt and the reply is thrown away unparsed). Minimal build: actually parse those labels against the ORBAT unit-id registry to get 'which units are tasked' - no prompt change at all, FLASH-cheap, and the preview-reuse path (ER-074) pays it once per decision. Limits: it runs PRE-adjudication, so it can name tasked units and proposed destinations but must not be authoritative for what happened (the quality verdict can nullify the action); str(dict) rendering of uk_forces should be replaced by the typed table for reliable id echo. Best used as the nomination stage feeding B.

D. Red-force movement through the inject YAML: add an optional 'movements:' list (unit_or_group, from, to, posture) beside 'effects:' in the inject schema (prompt at llm/prompts.py:458-468, parse at inject_generator.py:107-130, application beside apply_inject_effects sim_loop.py:188-295 with the same skip-and-record policy for unknown ids/locations). This is where red action already enters the world with structured, applied effects; the generator is player-facing (no Mystery secret) and PRO-tier. Also covers the facilitator seam for free IF deliver_inject routes the same primitive - but note deliver_inject deliberately skips the ledger, so spatial application there must be its own explicit step (game_manager.py:260-315).

E. Actor simulation, consuming: insert a FORCE DISPOSITIONS block into to_actor_context (models/narrative_state.py:352-359) or into build_actor_prompt's WORLD CONTEXT (actor_simulation.py:66-67) - but per-capital visibility filtering is required (a foreign government must not read UK readiness states it could not know; precedent: trust scores already stripped ER-014, and get_diplomatic_context's fail-closed whitelist ER-018 at context_builder.py:570-649 is the pattern). Emitting: an optional 'FORCE_POSTURE:'/'MOVEMENTS:' label on the actor reply, parsed in _parse_actor_response's existing style with default none, gives RUS/allies a voice in the spatial layer; calculate_effects_from_responses (actor_simulation.py:400-460) is the template for folding it into world effects. Caveat: identify_relevant_actors caps at 3 keyword-picked actors and RUS is not always in the roster (actor_simulation.py:347-397), so red movement cannot depend solely on this channel - D is the reliable red channel, E the flavour channel.

F. Where the table itself lives in prompts: render the unit-position table in the FAST-MOVING TAIL of build_shared_context_prefix (after the transcript, beside CURRENT SITUATION and the ledger, context_builder.py:416-439) - the ledger's placement note (ER-003) says exactly why: anything above the transcript that changes per turn destroys the cacheable prefix, and test_prompt_cache_order.py enforces it. For the non-dossier prompts (quality, actors), append the same rendered block to to_llm_context/to_actor_context so one renderer serves every family (mirror render_decisions_and_outcomes, narrative_state.py:286-309).
hazards: Seed-order/determinism: any task inserted BEFORE an existing task in a round's list shifts every child seed after it (decision_phase.py:151-194 pre-draw discipline); even appending changes the number of master-rng draws per round, so same-seed fresh campaigns replay differently across versions. Must append only, draw the new task's seed unconditionally (even when movement is disabled - the preview-reuse no-op-lambda trick at decision_phase.py:371-434 is the template), and accept a version fence: old saves resume correctly (rng_state serialized, restored after construction per ER-037 game_manager.py:936-940) but cross-version seed-42 golden transcripts change.

Mock-driver golden output churn: mock variant selection hashes the full prompt text (crc32, mock_driver.py:20-24), so ANY prompt edit - adding a unit table, a movement section, even a header line - silently reshuffles every canned advisor/actor/inject variant in mock campaigns. tests/test_mock_voices.py, test_decision_loop.py, test_turn_loop_integration.py and sim_loop.assert_determinism_seed_42 (sim_loop.py:885-889) are the blast radius; the mock driver also needs a canned MOVEMENT section or every offline/first-run campaign has a permanently static map.

Two-store sync trap generalises: metrics live twice (narrative_state.hidden_metrics is authoritative during adjudication; world.metrics is overwritten from it at resolve_decision game_manager.py:568-573, and briefing effects must be synced the OTHER way at game_manager.py:240-247 and deliver_inject:300-307). Put unit positions in ONE store only (WorldState is the right one - it is serialized whole and the facilitator seam already mutates it); if any spatial data ever mirrors into narrative_state the same silent-revert bug returns for positions.

Output-cap truncation ordering: quality assessment max_tokens=400, character responses 300 (narrative_adjudication.py:252,703). A movement section added to an existing reply is emitted AFTER the fields parsers need most, so truncation eats it first - or worse, reordering the prompt puts movement before EFFECTS and truncation eats the metric deltas. Any schema extension must raise the cap and keep new sections LAST; router truncation telemetry (router.py:123-137) will show the failure but not prevent it.

Fabrication-on-parse-failure: every family's contract is 'unreadable -> deterministic fallback, never invented content' (heuristic assessment, empty pushback, templated reactions, quiet-turn inject). Movement must inherit the conservative-closure principle stated at infer_event_disposition (narrative_adjudication.py:154-172): a false move (teleporting a carrier, un-mooring a unit that never sailed) is worse than a stale position. Unknown unit ids/locations must skip-and-record like apply_inject_effects' unknown-metric line (sim_loop.py:252-256,288-289), validated against the unit registry + gazetteer, never fuzzy-matched into the wrong hull.

Prompt-cache ordering is test-locked: the unit table changes every turn, so placing it above the transcript in build_shared_context_prefix breaks the append-only prefix property and fails tests/test_prompt_cache_order.py (and re-inflates per-call cost measured at issue #32: cacheable share 2.2% -> 75.9% when order was fixed). It must join the per-turn tail with CURRENT SITUATION and the ledger.

Save compatibility: a NEW pydantic field with default_factory loads old saves clean (the PlayedEvent ER-077 precedent); RETYPING spatial_state Dict[str,List[str]] is technically load-safe today only because no save ever contains a non-empty value - safer to add unit_positions and leave spatial_state dead or delete it in the same versioned change. pending_preview serialization (game_manager.py:851-857) means any movement data attached to the interpretation/preview must be JSON-native and keyed to exact action text or a save/load between interpret and commit desyncs orders from the committed decision.

Preview double-pay/staleness (ER-074): if movement nomination rides the interpretation call, the preview cache reuses it for identical text and correctly discards it for amended text - but round-2/3 movement resolution must re-read live positions, not preview-time positions, or a facilitator inject delivered between preview and commit (the EXCON seam is quiescent-period-legal) adjudicates against a stale map.

Player-facing leak surfaces: quality REASONING is displayed verbatim and the situation summary is quoted into later prompts (narrative_adjudication.py:189-235, 779-793 render effects only as direction words, never numbers). Movement truth entering these prompts will be narrated; hidden red positions (Mystery mode, red_objectives are 'hidden from Blue') must stay out of player-facing calls per the segregation rule at context_builder.py:407-411 - the spatial layer needs an explicit blue-visible / ground-truth split from day one.

Actor knowledge boundaries (ER-014/ER-018): feeding one shared position table to foreign-actor prompts leaks UK readiness to Moscow's roleplay and every capital's private posture to every other; a per-actor filtered rendering (the get_diplomatic_context fail-closed pattern) is required, which multiplies renderer variants and breaks the 'identical prefix' batching economics for the actor group.

Silent facilitator seam divergence: deliver_inject bypasses the ledger by design (game_manager.py:268-276) and would bypass any spatial application added only to the briefing/adjudication paths; conversely wiring spatial mutation into apply_inject_effects automatically gives the facilitator spatial power - decide explicitly, because effects applied only via world.metrics in that seam already need the hidden-metrics sync (game_manager.py:296-307) and a spatial analogue of that footgun is easy to recreate.

readers.summary: Saves serialize the ENTIRE WorldState via pydantic (v2, pinned 2.7.3) with default extra='ignore', through two parallel formats: engine/persistence.save_game ("world": model_dump(), version "2.4", rebuilt WorldState(**dict)) and GameManager.to_dict/from_dict ("state.world": world.dict(), rebuilt WorldState.parse_obj). Neither loader branches on version strings; missing keys take field defaults and unknown keys are silently dropped, so adding `spatial: Optional[SpatialState] = None` keeps every old save loadable in both directions — this is the codebase's own repeatedly-used migration idiom (recent_injects, event_ledger, rng_state, endings_disabled all landed this way with old-save tests). The dead spatial_state field has only ever serialized as {} (it is never written), so even retyping it would parse — but the honest move is to delete it (extra='ignore' makes removal save-safe; zero code reads it) and add a new typed field: SpatialState{version, units: Dict[str, UnitTrack{lat, lon, heading_deg, speed_kts, status, orders, destination, location_name, updated_turn}]}, matching the StateActorSystem precedent (nested pydantic model inside WorldState that round-trips with zero persistence code). Hydration belongs in GameManager._init_world, which already loads initial_conditions.yaml and builds WorldState — walk uk_forces (every unit has id/location/status) plus intelligence.russian_naval_deployment through a ~30-entry gazetteer YAML; get_resources then merges live world.spatial over the static YAML base (api ForceUnit needs Optional lat/lon added or FastAPI's response_model filter silently strips them). A purely deterministic kinematics step (dead reckoning, no rng draws) inside resolve_decision — after the pipeline, before turn++ — is determinism-safe because the danger is draw-sequence shift: batch LLM calls pre-draw child seeds from the session rng (decision_phase.py:166), so ANY new rng consumption diverges resumed old saves; if spatial randomness is ever wanted, derive an independent child generator, never tap self.rng. LLM-adjudicated unit updates must mutate world.spatial directly (the hidden_metrics copy-back trap covers only the five metric fields) and should use the labeled-line tolerant-parse format, not JSON. Test blast radius is small and well-mapped: prompt byte-parity goldens break only if spatial text renders unconditionally (render only when units exist and the parity fixture's empty world keeps parity), the GameManager vars()-introspection completeness test forces an explicit serialize-or-whitelist decision for any new manager attribute, and ~20 tests constructing WorldState by keyword are untouched by an optional defaulted field.
facts: Pydantic is pinned to 2.7.3 for the core game (requirements.txt: 'pydantic==2.7.3', with a comment that api/ deps live separately because fastapi pulls pydantic>=2.9); code uses v2 API (model_dump at engine/persistence.py:105) plus v1 shims (.dict() at engine/game_manager.py:836, .parse_obj at :921, .copy() at :149).

WorldState (models/world.py:20-67) declares NO model_config, so pydantic v2's default extra='ignore' applies: unknown keys in a save dict are silently dropped, missing keys take field defaults — adding an Optional-with-default field keeps old saves loadable AND lets old code load new saves.

Two parallel save formats serialize the whole WorldState: (a) CLI format — engine/persistence.py:105 '"world": world.model_dump()', version '2.4' at :119, loaded via WorldState(**world_dict) at :188; (b) GameManager format — engine/game_manager.py:836 'self.world.dict()' inside to_dict, loaded via WorldState.parse_obj(state['world']) at :921, written with json.dump(..., default=str) at :894.

No loader branches on the version string: persistence.load_game (:161-198) and read_save_field (:126-139) treat version as data; GameManager.from_dict (:899-979) never reads metadata.version — so a version bump to '2.5' is documentation, not a compatibility gate.

The additive-optional-field migration idiom is already used and tested repeatedly: recent_injects (models/world.py:52), event_ledger with explicit comment 'Absent from saves written before issue #25; defaults to empty so old campaigns load unchanged' (models/narrative_state.py:131-134), rng_state (tests/test_persistence.py:154-170 loads a pre-2.3 save), endings_disabled (tests/test_persistence.py:191-212).

spatial_state (models/world.py:40-43, Dict[str,List[str]]) is written by no code path repo-wide (grep: only docs/audits reference it; audits/2026-08-05-llm-context/data/agent-reports/synthesis.md:340 'Only occurrence repo-wide. Never written, never read'), so every existing save stores it as {} — meaning even retyping it to Dict[str,UnitTrack] would validate against real saves ({} parses under both types); removing it is also save-safe (extra='ignore' drops the stored key).

actor_system (models/world.py:64-67, Optional[StateActorSystem] = None) is the exact precedent for a nested mutable pydantic model inside WorldState that rides both save formats with zero persistence code; round-trip pinned by tests/test_saveload_completeness.py:113-120 test_actor_system_state_survives.

GameManager._init_world (engine/game_manager.py:105-155) already loads initial_conditions (:107) and constructs the WorldState (:121-136) — the natural hydration point; initial_conditions.yaml uk_forces entries each carry id/type/location/status (data/scenarios/war_game_2025/initial_conditions.yaml:120-260, e.g. HMS_Prince_of_Wales at Portsmouth, turns_to_full_readiness: 3), and the red fleet exists only as intelligence.russian_naval_deployment prose ('North Atlantic rendezvous point, moving southwest toward UK', 15 submarines).

get_resources (engine/game_manager.py:1018-1022) reads ONLY self.initial_conditions (static YAML), flattened by _flatten_forces/_build_force_summary (:1058-1088) which already emit id/branch/unit_type/location/status/readiness_turns — the merge point for live positions; the API response_model ForceUnit (api/server.py:358-367) has no lat/lon, and FastAPI's response_model filtering would silently strip any new keys until the model gains Optional fields.

self.initial_conditions is whitelisted as ephemeral in tests/test_saveload_completeness.py:26-33 EPHEMERAL_MANAGER_FIELDS ('static scenario data, reloaded from disk') — that vars()-introspection test (:79-91) fails CI for ANY new GameManager attribute that is neither serialized nor whitelisted with a reason.

readers.summary: VERDICT ON THE 5 QUESTIONS. (1) INJECT ENTRY PATHS — exactly three, all funnel through the same two primitives (display_inject + apply_inject_effects): [A] turn-briefing path (scripted episode file, else stochastic LLM generate_inject, else deterministic quiet-turn fallback) inside run_turn_briefing, invoked only by GameManager.get_turn_briefing; side-effects: ledger entry via record_played_event, narrator bridge, transcript lines, difficulty-scaled metric effects + clamp + flag recompute, recent_injects append (cap 5), mandatory-encounter handling, hidden-metrics sync, phase forced to discussion. [B] facilitator deliver_inject (POST /game/{sid}/inject, facilitator-flag gated, session-lock held): transcript lines, scaled effects, recent_injects, hidden-metrics sync ONLY when effect lines were produced — and deliberately NO ledger entry, no narrator bridge, no encounter, no phase change, no ending check; SSE emission is the caller's job (api/control.py). [C] the stochastic LLM generator is not a separate seam — it is path A's inject source; failures degrade to the quiet-turn inject, never to an error. (2) WHEN A TRIPWIRE CAN FIRE — the only legal instant is the turn boundary, concretely at the TOP of GameManager.get_turn_briefing (before run_turn_briefing), where the engine is provably quiescent and the post-movement spatial state is final (nothing moves between resolve_decision and the next briefing). Firing there puts the tripwire's transcript lines inside the LAST TURN continuity window the same turn's inject generator slices (get_last_turn_slice cuts from the previous TURN header, and the header for the new turn is written after the hook point), so the LLM builds the turn's event ON the crossing; advisors/decision/omissions then see it all turn. Mid-turn via deliver_inject is structurally broken for a system tripwire: no ledger entry is possible (adjudication closes ledger[-1]), the situation-summary fold never sees it (fold prompt reads only ledger[-1].title + decision + outcome, never the transcript), endings cannot fire until the next resolve_decision anyway, the per-session SSE queue is a destructive work-queue so mid-turn pushes can be lost to a second consumer, and a mid-turn save/load can refire it unless a fired-tripwire registry is serialized. The briefing hook must be replay-guarded (skip when the ER-004 replay flag is set) and idempotent via a fired-tripwires set stored on WorldState. Tripwire-triggered ENDINGS should be deferred: check_ending is called only in resolve_decision before turn-advance, and calling it at briefing time (turn already advanced) would mis-grade the final turn — accept the same one-turn latency scripted briefing effects already have. (3) REACHING THE LLM — four existing channels, use all of them: (a) transcript lines via the deliver-style primitives → build_shared_context_prefix reaches every advisor/decision/pushback/omissions prompt but decays with window elision; (b) recent_injects title append → reaches ONLY build_critical_omissions_prompt; (c) the event ledger → reaches both the shared dossier (DECISIONS AND OUTCOMES via to_llm_context and render_event_ledger in the prefix) and the inject generator (EVENTS ALREADY PLAYED + do-not-restage rule 8) — this is the only durable memory, so the tripwire MUST get a ledger entry (see 4); (d) a new SPATIAL PICTURE/TRIPWIRE block appended in build_shared_context_prefix's fast-moving tail (after the CURRENT SITUATION metrics, NEVER above the transcript — the prefix-cache ordering is load-bearing) is the right home for the authoritative typed positions themselves, and the same block handed to build_inject_generation_prompt as mandatory facts lets the generator narrate around deterministic truth. The adjudicator sees it through narrative_state.to_llm_context's ledger block plus the new spatial block. (4) LEDGER — deliver_inject's skip is SEMANTICS for facilitator one-offs (record_event_disposition closes ledger[-1]; record_played_event overwrites by turn number; the ledger is structurally one player-adjudicated event per turn) but it is a GAP for system tripwires: a non-ledger event vanishes from the fold and from EVENTS ALREADY PLAYED, so the generator can restage the crossing as a fresh discovery — the exact issue-#25 failure class the ledger exists to prevent. The honest fix under the new framing is a small model change: add kind: Literal["played","system"] to PlayedEvent (default "played" so old saves load clean), make record_event_disposition close the last kind=="played" entry and record_played_event overwrite only same-turn+same-kind; then tripwires enter the ledger without misdirecting the turn verdict. Tests test_inject_seam.py and test_event_ledger.py encode the current invariant and must be updated deliberately. (5) ENDINGS & MYSTERY — check_ending is pure over metrics+turn, so tripwire metric effects route into it automatically at the next adjudication; but ending prose is static and geography-flavored ('The submarines are returning north'), so an authoritative spatial layer can contradict the verdict text — a later opt-in change could condition resolution/uneasy_peace on a spatial predicate. Tripwires must no-op once manager.ending is set. Mystery Mode is safe on the leak side ONLY if movement updates derive exclusively from player-visible events: the hidden NarrativeConfig reaches roleplay prompts alone (the segregation IS the leak defence), and a deterministic tripwire uses no LLM and no secret — but if unit MOVEMENT were ever conditioned on the drawn narrative, the globe becomes a side channel that lets a player infer the hidden truth from geometry. Movement must obey the same segregation rule as prompts. Also: the Mystery draw burns constructor RNG that from_dict replays before restoring state, so the tripwire/movement machinery must be RNG-free pure geometry or the save format's ER-037 contract breaks.

designs.name: TASKORD — Orders-Not-Positions Spatial Authority
designs.thesis: The LLM never touches a coordinate. It emits MOVEMENT ORDERS — structured intent (unit_id, mission enum, gazetteer destination or coarse bearing, speed band enum) — in one dedicated, cheap, appended round-3 call plus optional `movements:` lists on injects. A pure, RNG-free kinematics module (engine/kinematics.py) advances typed lat/lon UnitTracks from those orders exactly once per resolve_decision, and the between-turn ambient daemon interpolates along the SAME kinematics functions, so the globe renders the engine's own truth projected forward, never fiction. Garbage-coordinate risk is eliminated by construction: validation is set-membership (unit registry, gazetteer, enums) plus domain speed caps, and every failure degrades to standing-order dead reckoning — the map can go stale, but it can never lie, teleport, or freeze.

designs.movement: WHO DECIDES: the LLM decides INTENT, the engine decides GEOMETRY. Stage 1 — order emission (LLM): a new task `movement_orders` APPENDED (append-only, never inserted) to round 3 of run_decision_pipeline (decision_phase.py:492-505, mirrored in narrative_adjudication._run_reactions_and_summary_round:944-979 for the CLI path). Round 3 today holds 2 tasks against MAX_ROUND_WORKERS=3 (decision_phase.py:91), so the call is zero wall-clock; it gets its own LLMContext.MOVEMENT family (llm/model_config.py, FLASH tier — the task is constrained selection, not prose), its own parse-health bucket, its own call-log identity. Its child seed is drawn UNCONDITIONALLY even when movement is disabled (the preview no-LLM-lambda trick, decision_phase.py:371-434) so seed draws never shift within a version. Inputs (richest point in the turn): rendered unit table + gazetteer id list + committed action + interpretation + quality verdict + applied final_effects + parsed actor stances; NEVER the Mystery narrative. Optional free nomination: parse the interpretation call's already-requested-but-discarded FORCES INVOLVED label (data/prompts/decision_interpretation.txt; reply currently thrown away, conversation.py:358) against the unit registry to pre-highlight tasked units — pre-adjudication, advisory only. Stage 2 — kinematics advance (deterministic): NEW engine/kinematics.py, pure `advance(spatial, gazetteer, dt_hours)` — no Random, no wall clock, fits the deterministic_midpoint/compute_risk_flags house idiom (rules.py:23-32, flags.py). Runs inside resolve_decision AFTER pipeline sync (game_manager.py:566-574) and BEFORE turn++ (:589-593), with fixed dt_hours per turn from scenario config (e.g. 12h): great-circle step toward destination at the speed-band→knots table per domain (surface cruise 18kt / flank 28; sub slow 8 / cruise 15; air transit 420), clamp to domain max, snap to location_name inside the gazetteer arrival radius (mission→hold, speed→0); bearing orders advance along the bearing with a hard per-turn distance cap. Units the LLM ordered this turn → provenance 'adjudicated'; units advancing standing/doctrine orders → 'simulated'. RED FORCES move by default doctrine — a scripted leg list (North_Atlantic_rendezvous → GIUK_gap → UK_waters) stored as scenario_init standing orders, keyed by inject id not turn number (fast_start renumbering hazard, XR doc §4) — overridable by inject `movements:` and by the round-3 call reacting to VISIBLE events only. VALIDATION (every order, every source, no exceptions): unit_id exact-∈ spatial.units (never fuzzy-matched into the wrong hull) → mission/speed ∈ enum via match_enum → destination exact-∈ gazetteer XOR bearing ∈ [0,360) → domain legality (air units cannot 'patrol' at sea-only ids without base range, v2). Any failure: drop that order, record_miss, visible transcript line 'Skipped: unknown unit X' (the sim_loop.py:288 unknown-metric template). DETERMINISM ACCOUNTING, stated honestly: kinematics draws zero rng; the appended round-3 task raises the master-rng draw count from 2 to 3 for that round, so same-seed FRESH campaigns diverge across code versions from round 3 of turn 1 — a documented version fence; in-version determinism, saved-rng resumes (rng_state restored post-construction, game_manager.py:933-940), and assert_determinism_seed_42 within a version are all preserved; cross-version goldens are re-goldened once, deliberately.
designs.llm_contract: EMISSION SCHEMA (house style: labelled plain-text lines parsed by llm/parsing.py primitives — the repo's documented parse-fragility verdict rules out JSON): the round-3 MOVEMENT call (max_tokens 250) returns either the standalone sentinel `NO_ORDERS` or up to 8 lines of `ORDER: <unit_id> | mission=<enum> | dest=<gazetteer_id> | speed=<band>` (or `bearing=<0-359>` in place of dest). Parser: per-line extract_label('ORDER'), split on '|', match_enum for mission/speed with negation lookback, exact set-membership for unit_id/dest, find_signed_int range-checked for bearing; lines beyond 8 recorded as residue; each bad line skipped + record_miss under the MOVEMENT family. SECOND CHANNEL (reliable red input): the inject YAML gains an optional `movements:` list (`- {unit: RED_SSN_group, mission: transit, dest: GIUK_gap, speed: cruise}`) beside `effects:` — prompt schema extended at llm/prompts.py:458-470, parsed in inject_generator.py's yaml.safe_load path with the same tolerant skip-and-record policy, applied by a new sim_loop.apply_spatial_orders sibling of apply_inject_effects; deliver_inject routes the same key as an explicit step (mutates world.spatial, records NO ledger entry per the seam rule at game_manager.py:269-275), giving the facilitator physics-respecting spatial power for free. THIRD (flavour-only): an optional FORCE_POSTURE label on actor replies, parsed default-none in _parse_actor_response style — never load-bearing, since identify_relevant_actors caps at 3 and RUS isn't guaranteed present. CONSUMPTION: one renderer, render_spatial_picture() (~20-30 lines, ~500-800 tokens: `HMS_Prince_of_Wales | carrier | en-route GIUK_gap | transit/cruise | ETA 2 turns` + 'crossed GIUK_gap this turn' tripwire annotations), appended in the FAST-MOVING TAIL of build_shared_context_prefix (after the transcript, beside CURRENT SITUATION and the ledger — test_prompt_cache_order.py's cacheable-prefix invariant is load-bearing, context_builder.py:378-395) and appended to to_llm_context for the quality assessment; the inject generator gets the same block as mandatory-facts-to-narrate-around in get_stochastic_inject_context; player-facing calls receive the BLUE-plus-estimates rendering, the movement call alone receives red truth (its output is orders, not prose — nothing player-visible leaks). FULL DEGRADATION LADDER, per turn: (1) clean parse → orders applied → kinematics → 'adjudicated'; (2) partial parse → valid lines applied, bad lines skipped + record_miss + visible transcript line; (3) empty reply / '[ERROR:' batch slot / router mock-substitution after one retry (router.py:380-393) / truncation (finish_reason telemetry, router.py:123-137) → ZERO new orders, record_fallback, every unit continues its standing order and kinematics still advances — provenance 'simulated'; (4) movement feature-flagged off, or mock driver without the new MOVEMENT handler → permanent case-3: the map runs pure doctrine projection (red still closes on the UK, blue holds station) — moving, honest, never adjudicated; (5) kinematics cannot fail nondeterministically — a unit with no order and no doctrine HOLDS (conservative closure per narrative_adjudication.py:154-172: a stale position beats a false move, always). Because MOVEMENT is its own call, there is no truncation-ordering conflict with the quality call's EFFECTS fields and no raise of its max_tokens=400 — the two known regression traps of the piggyback alternative are avoided by construction.

WHEN: exactly one legal instant — the top of GameManager.get_turn_briefing (engine/game_manager.py:182, before the run_turn_briefing call), the provably quiescent point where post-kinematics positions are final; firing there writes the tripwire's lines into manager.transcript BEFORE run_turn_briefing writes the new TURN header, so they land inside the LAST TURN slice (llm/prompts.py:408-416) and the same turn's inject generator builds the turn's event ON the crossing, while every advisor/decision/pushback/omissions prompt sees it all turn via the shared dossier. Mid-turn firing is structurally rejected (destructive SSE work-queue, no ledger slot, fold blindness — per the seam study). DELIVERY: through the deliver-style primitives — display_inject lines, apply_inject_effects (difficulty scaling + clamp + flag recompute), recent_injects append, AND the hidden-metrics sync (the game_manager.py:296-307 pattern, applied unconditionally when effects exist — replicating deliver_inject's effects-without-sync half is the exact silent-revert bug); plus a LEDGER entry via the small model change: PlayedEvent gains kind:Literal['played','system']='played' (old saves load clean via default), record_event_disposition (narrative_adjudication.py:140) closes the last kind=='played' entry, record_played_event overwrites only same-turn+same-kind — so crossings durably enter EVENTS ALREADY PLAYED (no issue-#25 restaging) and DECISIONS AND OUTCOMES without absorbing the player's turn verdict; tests test_inject_seam.py:92-100 and test_event_ledger.py pin the old invariant and are updated in the same commit. GUARDS: fired ids persisted in SpatialState.fired_tripwires (a mid-turn save/load cannot refire); skip entirely under the ER-004 replay flag (mirror game_manager.py:189-190); no-op once manager.ending is set; scenario-load validation evaluates every predicate against initial hydration and rejects any that fires before its not_before_turn (the red fleet already AT North_Atlantic_rendezvous must not fire a turn-1 volley). Ending effects route through metrics into check_ending at the NEXT resolve_decision — the same one-turn latency scripted briefing effects already have, accepted rather than mis-grading final_turn. PLAYER/FACILITATOR SURFACING: extend the briefing_events mapper (api/server.py:141-157, shared by the HTTP endpoint and api/demo.py) — get_turn_briefing returns inject['system_events']=[…]; one transcript SSE per firing on layer_for_channel of its channel ('flash_alert'/'military'→SITREP, 'intelligence'→INTEL) plus a raw geometric record (unit, zone, range) on Layer.REFEREE, server-side filtered from player streams (server.py:823-831). Concrete scenario set: red group zone_entry GIUK_gap (flash_alert, escalation_risk+4); closing_within 200nm of Faslane (intelligence); range_ring 400nm of London ~ Kalibr envelope (military); blue carrier zone_entry GIUK_gap (REFEREE-only, feeds red doctrine reaction).
designs.globe_binding: The globe consumes ONLY engine truth or deterministic derivations of it, stamped with provenance on every frame. (1) API of record: get_resources (game_manager.py:1018-1129) merges live world.spatial over the static YAML flatten per unit id — live location_name/lat/lon/heading/speed/provenance override, static branch/armament retained; api ForceUnit (server.py:358-367) gains Optional lat/lon/heading_deg/speed_kts/provenance or FastAPI response_model filtering silently strips them (a no-error failure — pinned by a new test). engine/intelligence.py's fabricated ranges (:196-199, rng.randint '150-250nm') are rewired to read the estimate layer — otherwise the INTEL channel visibly lies against the globe it now shares truth with. (2) AMBIENT DAEMON UPGRADE (the prior study's stream-only api/geo_sim.py, XR doc:58): it keeps everything that made it safe — own thread, never takes session.lock, never mutates engine state, own RNG for decoration, per-subscriber fan-out on a dedicated /geo/stream — but its keyframe source flips from scripted fiction to truth: at each turn boundary resolve_decision publishes an immutable deep-copied SpatialSnapshot (spatial dict + turn + standing orders) into a latest-wins thread-safe mailbox on GameSession; between snapshots the daemon calls THE SAME engine/kinematics.advance() at fractional dt to interpolate every unit along its standing order across however long the real turn takes (sim_clock slew ratio) — so the ambient picture is the truth's own forward projection, marked provenance 'simulated'. On snapshot arrival, where adjudication contradicts the interpolation, SLEW-NOT-TELEPORT is retained verbatim: decay the correction over 30-90s, presented diegetically as an intelligence-picture refresh; post-correction frames carry 'adjudicated'. (3) DTDL PROVENANCE: the parse-clean TheatreAsset interface (14 interfaces/309 entities in Microsoft's DTDLParser) gains two fields — `provenance` enum {adjudicated: position written by the kinematics step from an LLM-issued or inject/facilitator order this turn; simulated: doctrine/standing-order dead-reckoning or between-turn interpolation; estimated: fog-filtered fix served to the player} — and `sourceTurn:int`; the REFEREE stream and any ADT upload carry truth+provenance, the player twin carries estimates, and the HUD badges the prior study planned render the ladder directly. (4) FOG-OF-WAR: NEW engine/intel_picture.py — blue own-force renders as truth; red units render to the player as ESTIMATE = last confirmed fix + error offset whose radius grows with turns-since-last_confirmed_turn and collapses when the unit sits inside a blue sensor footprint (P-8 squadron at Lossiemouth airborne → North Atlantic coverage ring; Type-23 towed array radius; SSN trail); the offset comes from a DERIVED generator Random(hash((seed, unit_id, turn, 'fog'))) — never self.rng (the decision_phase.py:166 child-seed draw sequence is sacred), deterministic per save so a reload renders the identical estimate. Player subscribers of /geo/stream and /resources get the estimate + uncertainty radius; facilitator (session.facilitator-gated, the control.py:157-161 pattern) gets truth with the player-estimate overlay. MYSTERY-MODE SIDE CHANNEL, closed by rule: red movement derives ONLY from player-visible events (injects, doctrine legs, adjudicated outcomes) — never from the hidden NarrativeConfig, and the movement call never receives it — so geometry cannot be mined to read the drawn secret. WHAT STAYS DECORATIVE, permanently, by design: civil air/shipping corridors, satellite passes, sensor-shader cosmetics and camera grammar (pure geo_sim, own RNG, never persisted); sub-turn interpolated micro-positions (derived, never written back — persisted truth is turn-boundary state only); t_plus/sim_clock stamps (presentation-only, per _make_item); abstract-location units ('classified' SSBN, 'available' Astutes) which have no coordinates and are never rendered; ending prose geography (endings stay pure over metrics in v1 — a cosmetic post-ending 'rtb north' doctrine order reconciles 'the submarines are returning north' with the map without touching scoring); and the player's uncertainty ellipses, which are a view, not state.

designs.effort: Solo dev with LLM assistance, staged so every stage ships playable alone. Stage A (models/spatial.py, gazetteer.yaml, kinematics, hydration, red doctrine legs, resolve_decision wiring, save round-trip tests): ~5-7 days — already yields a moving truth-map with zero LLM involvement. Stage B (round-3 MOVEMENT call, parser, prompt block renderer, mock handler, re-golden): ~4-5 days. Stage C (tripwires + PlayedEvent.kind ledger change + briefing_events SSE + test updates): ~4-6 days. Stage D (fog/intel_picture, get_resources/ForceUnit merge, intelligence.py rewire): ~3-4 days. Stage E (geo_sim.py truth-fed daemon + fan-out + slew reconciliation — the prior study's judged 2-3x multiplier applies here, fan-out plumbing dominates): ~5-8 days. Stage F (DTDL provenance fields + parser revalidation): ~1-2 days. Total ~4-6 working weeks part-time, ~3 weeks focused; the risk-weighted core (A+B) is under two weeks.
risks: Any prompt-text change (unit table, new sections) reshuffles mock_driver crc32 variant selection — every mock golden (test_mock_voices, test_decision_loop, assert_determinism_seed_42) churns at once; must land as one deliberate re-golden commit, and without a canned MOVEMENT handler all offline/mock campaigns run doctrine-only maps forever

Appending the round-3 task changes master-rng draws (2→3), so same-seed fresh campaigns diverge across code versions from turn 1 round 3 — in-version determinism and rng_state resumes survive, but the version fence must be documented and cross-version golden transcripts abandoned

Expressiveness ceiling of orders-not-positions: the LLM can only route units to ~30 gazetteer ids or coarse bearings — a novel mid-ocean ambush point is inexpressible; bearing orders are the pressure valve, gazetteer growth the roadmap, and this ceiling is the deliberate price of zero coordinate hallucination

Two-store trap recurrence: any cache of positions in narrative_state, geo_sim daemon state treated as authority, or a facilitator effect applied without the hidden-metrics sync recreates the silent-revert class — enforced by the single-store rule, read-only snapshots, and a dedicated regression test, but it is a standing discipline, not a one-time fix
FastAPI response_model filtering strips undeclared ForceUnit fields with no error anywhere — a globe that renders nothing while every test passes; pinned by an explicit serialization test

Fog noise or any spatial randomness accidentally tapping self.rng shifts the child-seed sequence and corrupts resumed saves — the derived-generator rule (Random(hash((seed,unit_id,turn,'fog')))) must be enforced in review, it cannot be enforced by type

Quality-assessment REASONING is shown to the player verbatim: the spatial block fed to player-facing calls must be the blue+estimates rendering, never red truth, or the model narrates hidden positions — a per-call-audience renderer split that is easy to get wrong once and leak once

designs.name: IRONCLAD — Doctrine State Machine Spatial Layer (zero-LLM movement loop, closed-enum orders)
designs.thesis: Movement is never generated, only selected. Every unit runs an authored doctrine program (patrol box, transit leg, QRA alert, readying-in-port, shadow, withdraw) defined in a per-scenario doctrine pack; a pure, RNG-free engine tick advances positions along authored routes once per committed decision. The LLM's entire spatial role is picking transitions from a menu the engine prints into the prompt — the exact enum-echo pattern the codebase already trusts for QUALITY (5-way), OUTCOME (3-way) and WILL_SUPPORT, parsed by the existing match_enum/extract_label/parse_health stack. Result: byte-replayable movement, property-testable geometry, a fail-safe where LLM failure means 'standing orders continue' (patrols keep patrolling) instead of a frozen or hallucinated map, and a red fleet that closes on the UK as a deterministic, dread-inducing clock the globe renders as truth. The honest cost, stated up front: expressiveness is capped at what the scenario author encoded — novel maneuvers the doctrine pack lacks are visibly refused, never improvised.

designs.movement: WHO DECIDES: the engine, deterministically — the LLM never moves anything, it only selects orders (see llm_contract). WHEN: exactly once per committed decision, inside resolve_decision after the pipeline result and hidden-metrics copy-back (game_manager.py:566-574) and before check_ending/turn++ (:586-593), so the ledger, ending check and next briefing all see the moved world. Previews (ER-074) never tick — movement is commit-only, preventing double-advance; a facilitator inject between preview and commit is fine because orders are applied against live positions at commit. HOW: NEW engine/spatial_engine.py advance_spatial(spatial, validated_orders, sim_hours) — a pure function in the house style of rules.deterministic_midpoint and flags.compute_risk_flags: zero RNG (never touches self.rng — the decision_phase.py:166 child-seed pre-draw makes any new draw corrupt resumed saves per ER-037), zero wall-clock. Steps: (1) apply validated posture transitions (each order = unit_id × posture × optional gazetteer destination); (2) advance each unit along its posture program: transit legs consume speed_kts × sim_hours_per_turn nm along the authored route polyline; patrol postures hold a deterministic racetrack point in their named box; in-port/QRA postures decrement readiness_turns_remaining (the carrier's turns_to_full_readiness:3 from initial_conditions.yaml becomes live state); (3) recompute location_name by gazetteer-area containment; (4) run the deterministic sensor model to regenerate ContactEstimates (P-8 posture on-station + escalation band → fix quality; error_radius_nm grows per turn since last fix; display offset = bounded hash(track_id, turn) inside the error circle — deterministic noise, no RNG); (5) stamp provenance: 'adjudicated' on units whose posture changed by an applied order this turn, 'simulated' on pure dead-reckoning, 'facilitator' on EXCON edits. RED MOVEMENT: Operation Tuman is an authored plan graph (rendezvous → SW transit → GIUK penetration → UK-waters holding → strike posture); phase transitions fire deterministically from turn windows and escalation_risk bands (the flags.py precedent), and can be overridden by inject 'orders:' directives or a clamped actor FORCE_POSTURE label — but never depend on the LLM, so red always closes on schedule even fully offline. VALIDATION (conservative closure, per the infer_event_disposition principle at narrative_adjudication.py:154-172 — a stale position beats a false one): unit id must exact-match the registry (NO fuzzy matching into the wrong hull); posture must be an edge in that unit's transition graph FROM its current posture (the graph enforces escalation ordering — red cannot jump rendezvous→strike); destination must be a gazetteer name legal for that posture; violations skip-and-record_miss with a visible REFEREE transcript line ('Order refused: SSN_Astute_1 cannot STRIKE from IN_PORT'), mirroring apply_inject_effects' unknown-metric line (sim_loop.py:288). No teleports exist outside the facilitator primitive. HYDRATION: _init_world (game_manager.py:105-155) walks uk_forces (18 typed units, all carrying id/location/status already) + red_plan phase 0 through the gazetteer into UnitTracks.
designs.llm_contract: ONE new call family, LLMContext.POSTURE_SELECTION, FLASH tier (~10 lines in llm/model_config.py), appended as the THIRD task of round 3 (decision_phase.py:492-505, mirrored in _run_reactions_and_summary_round for the CLI path) — zero wall-clock cost since round 3 runs 2 tasks against MAX_ROUND_WORKERS=3, and the richest inputs (committed action, interpretation, quality verdict, applied effects) are in hand. APPEND-ONLY with an unconditional seed draw even when spatial is disabled (the preview no-op-lambda trick at decision_phase.py:371-434), preserving in-version determinism; the extra master-RNG draw is a documented version fence — old saves resume correctly (rng_state restored, game_manager.py:933-940) but cross-version seed-42 goldens re-golden once. PROMPT: the engine prints an ORDER MENU it computed deterministically — per blue unit one line: 'SSN_Astute_1 | TRANSIT(Faslane) | legal: HOLD, TRANSIT->{GIUK_gap, North_Atlantic, Portsmouth}, PATROL{UK_waters}' — plus the committed action, interpretation, and quality verdict. ~25 lines, ~700 tokens; NOT added to any existing prompt, so the quality assessment's 400-token cap and player-facing REASONING are untouched. OUTPUT (house labeled-line style, never JSON — the documented parse-fragility rule): 'ORDERS:' then one 'unit_id: ORDER_TOKEN [destination]' per line, sentinel 'NO_ORDERS' for quiet turns; max_tokens 300 with ORDERS as the only content so truncation cannot eat trailing fields. Parsed by extract_label + exact registry match on unit + match_enum against THAT UNIT'S printed menu + exact gazetteer match on destination. DEGRADATION LADDER (full): (1) one line unparseable → skip line, record_miss('posture_selection'); (2) legal-syntax/illegal-transition → skip, record_miss, REFEREE 'order refused' transcript line; (3) empty reply, '[ERROR:' slot, or task exception → no orders this turn, record_fallback — every unit continues STANDING DOCTRINE (transits keep transiting, patrols keep patrolling, red plan advances regardless), so the map never freezes and nothing is fabricated; (4) router-level failure → MockDeterministicDriver substitution (router.py:380-393) whose new POSTURE_SELECTION handler (llm/mock_driver.py) returns NO_ORDERS (or scripted canned orders for demo campaigns), keeping offline/mock play deterministic; (5) truncation → router telemetry records it (router.py:123-137), partial lines parse individually. RED CHANNELS: optional 'orders:' list in inject YAML beside 'effects:' (prompt llm/prompts.py:458-468, parse inject_generator.py:107-130, applied via a new apply_spatial_orders sibling of apply_inject_effects with identical skip-and-record policy) — the reliable channel; optional FORCE_POSTURE label on the RUS actor reply parsed in _parse_actor_response style, default none, clamped to at most one legal plan-phase advance — flavour only, since identify_relevant_actors doesn't guarantee RUS in the roster. CONSUMPTION: a compact SPATIAL PICTURE block (blue truth + red contact ESTIMATES, ~15 aggregated lines) rendered by one shared renderer into the fast-moving tail of build_shared_context_prefix (after the transcript, beside CURRENT SITUATION — test_prompt_cache_order.py-safe) and appended to to_llm_context; rendered ONLY when world.spatial exists, keeping the prompt-parity golden green on the empty fixture world. Actor prompts get NO spatial block in v1 (fail-closed, the ER-014/ER-018 rule); per-capital filtered views are a later opt-in. The inject generator receives the same block as mandatory facts to narrate AROUND — it decorates deterministic truth, never decides it. HONEST ENUM-RELIABILITY ASSESSMENT: precedent is real but smaller — QUALITY/OUTCOME/WILL_SUPPORT are single 3-5-way enums per reply; this is a joint selection (unit × posture × destination) across ~18 units, combinatorially the largest parsed output in the game. Menu-echo (the legal answers are printed in the prompt) is materially easier than free generation and parse_health gives day-one miss-rate telemetry — but a wrong-yet-legal order (tasking Type23_Frigate_2 when the player meant _1) validates cleanly; the syntactic gate cannot catch semantic errors. Mitigations: menu lines carry current location/status as disambiguators, orders echo into the REFEREE layer for facilitator veto, and the deliberate bias is inaction (skip) over wrong action.
designs.tripwires: Authored geometric predicates in doctrine.yaml: {id, when: crosses(named_line e.g. GIUK_line) | enters(named_area e.g. UK_waters_200nm) | range_lt(of: unit_class, nm: e.g. red SSN within Sea Viper envelope of any Type45's live position — computable precisely because both sides' truth is typed), channel, effects[], headline_template, not_before_turn, once:true, visibility: detected|always}. WHEN THEY FIRE: evaluated by pure geometry (no RNG, no LLM, no wall clock) at the TOP of GameManager.get_turn_briefing (engine/game_manager.py:182, before run_turn_briefing at :192) — the one provably quiescent instant where post-movement state is final. Guards: skip under the ER-004 replay flag (:189-190 pattern); idempotence via the serialized fired_tripwires registry; not_before_turn linted at scenario load against initial positions so turn 1 cannot open with a spurious volley (red already starts at North_Atlantic_rendezvous heading SW — the GIUK crossing is authored to fire around turn 3-4 of the plan); no-op once manager.ending is set. HOW THEY REACH THE LLM AND PLAYER: delivered through the deliver_inject primitives (display_inject + apply_inject_effects + recent_injects + hidden-metrics sync, game_manager.py:285-307) BEFORE run_turn_briefing, so the transcript lines land inside the LAST TURN window the same turn's inject generator slices (get_last_turn_slice cuts from the previous TURN header, written after the hook point) — the generator builds the turn's event ON the crossing — and every advisor/decision/pushback/omissions dossier carries it all turn. Durable memory via the ledger kind-field change (PlayedEvent gains kind:Literal['played','system']='played'; record_event_disposition closes the last kind=='played' entry, record_played_event overwrites same-turn+same-kind — models/narrative_state.py:46-73, narrative_adjudication.py:140, :394-405), so crossings enter EVENTS ALREADY PLAYED and the situation-summary fold without absorbing the player's turn verdict; tests test_inject_seam.py:92-100 and test_event_ledger.py updated deliberately in the same commit. On scripted-exhausted turns a firing tripwire BECOMES the turn's inject through path A itself (fed as a deterministic inject dict where sim_loop.py:379-399 would fall back to the quiet turn), replacing 'no significant developments' printed while a fleet crosses a line; effects always apply deterministically, LLM generation only decorates. Player surfacing: SSE via the briefing_events mapper (api/server.py:141-157) extended to emit one transcript event per tripwire on layer_for_channel plus a raw geometric record on Layer.REFEREE — fired at the briefing boundary where the client is actively draining, sidestepping the destructive work-queue loss mode. FOG-CONSISTENT FIRING: visibility:'detected' tripwires fire the player-facing inject only when the ContactEstimate supports detection (fix fresh enough, error radius small enough — deterministic check); the REFEREE/facilitator record always fires on truth; an undetected crossing surfaces later as a delayed, ambiguous intel inject when a fix is regained. Tripwire-triggered endings accept the existing one-turn latency (check_ending runs only in resolve_decision pre-advance; calling it at briefing would mis-grade final_turn).
designs.globe_binding: The globe stops rendering fiction and binds to world.spatial as TRUTH, with the prior study's stream-only api/geo_sim.py daemon UPGRADED from fabricator to renderer/interpolator: it still never takes session.lock and never mutates engine state, but instead of scripted fictional track legs it consumes immutable truth SNAPSHOTS deep-copied at exactly the two mutation points (end of resolve_decision's tick; end of get_turn_briefing's tripwire/inject application) — never mid-mutation reads. Between snapshots it SLEWS each track from previous to current authoritative position ALONG THE UNIT'S ACTUAL DOCTRINE ROUTE LEGS (which it can read from the doctrine pack — a unique advantage of this design: the interpolation path is the true path, not a straight line through Ireland), stretched across however long the real turn takes — slew-not-teleport preserved. Reconciliation rule: catch-up speed capped at 3x doctrine speed; divergence beyond a threshold (a facilitator teleport) cuts with an explicit 'track re-designated' event rather than sliding a carrier across land. The daemon keeps its own seeded RNG for ambient-only content and its own per-subscriber fan-out queues (never the destructive session queue). DTDL PROVENANCE LADDER: the proven-parse-clean TheatreAsset interface gains telemetry position{lat,lon}/headingDeg/speedKts/posture and properties provenance:enum{simulated, estimated, adjudicated} + errorRadiusNm + sourceTurn (re-verified in DTDLParser). Mapping: dead-reckoned doctrine positions = 'simulated'; positions set/confirmed by an applied order or facilitator/EXCON action that turn = 'adjudicated'; the player's red picture = 'estimated' (from ContactEstimate, carrying errorRadiusNm + confidence). The daemon's intra-turn interpolations inherit the underlying sample's provenance plus an interpolated flag; HUD badges render the ladder (the DTMI-badge grammar from XR_GLOBE_FEASIBILITY). FOG-OF-WAR AT EMIT TIME: facilitator subscribers receive truth tracks for both sides PLUS an overlay of the player's estimate layer — the visible gap between them IS the deception game for EXCON; player subscribers receive blue truth (own forces) and ONLY ContactEstimates for red (truth + deterministic bounded noise, error circles growing with turns since last fix — degraded further when the player re-tasks the P-8s away from patrol), and never receive kind:abstract units. WHAT STAYS DECORATIVE EVEN NOW: ambient civil air/sea corridors, satellite passes, sensor-cone shaders, weather, camera cinematics, all VFX (EXERCISE-labeled per the honest-labeling rule); sub-turn interpolated positions and t_plus timing (presentation only — truth exists ONLY at turn-boundary snapshots); kind:abstract units ('classified' SSBN on patrol, 'available' Astutes before tasking) render as badges, never dots — the deterrent's whole point is that even the truth layer doesn't know where it is; the interpretation call's FORCES INVOLVED prose stays narrative; intelligence.py's fabricated 'holding 150-250nm' ranges are DELETED and rewired to read ContactEstimates, and get_resources merges live spatial — otherwise both would visibly lie against the authoritative globe.

designs.name: CARTOGRAPHER: async world-simulator spatial layer
designs.thesis: Truth advances in two tiers that never block the game loop: a synchronous, RNG-free dead-reckoning step inside resolve_decision guarantees positions always move plausibly, and an out-of-band single-LLM 'cartographer' pass (spawned via asyncio.create_task at api/server.py:1104/:1043 right after resolve_decision returns, running the sync router call in asyncio.to_thread) reads the committed turn outcome and emits a hard-validated labelled-line spatial delta that REFINES the dead-reckoned prediction — including spawning color entities the ORBAT never listed (a shadowing AGI ship, a P-8 patrol line) under strict caps. The briefing never waits: if the delta hasn't committed by the next POST /briefing, the turn proceeds on dead reckoning and the delta merges late or is fenced off. Because the cartographer is a NEW LLM family with its own prompt and draws zero seeds from the session RNG, it adds authoritative movement without shifting a single existing child seed, reshuffling a single mock-driver crc32 variant, or touching any prompt-parity golden — the entire feature is flag-gated (`spatial.enabled` in scenario YAML) and additive.

designs.effort: Solo dev with LLM assistance: ~15-19 focused days (~3-4 part-time weeks), in five independently-shippable phases. P1 typed state + gazetteer + hydration + dead reckoning + get_resources merge + save round-trip tests: 3-4 days (mostly mechanical; the gazetteer itself is the verified afternoon's work). P2 cartographer call + validation ladder + commit gate + mock handler + parse tests: 4-5 days (the heaviest single item — the validation burden is the price of my angle — but it reuses llm/parsing.py and the parse-health registry wholesale). P3 tripwires + PlayedEvent kind field + briefing_events mapper + seam-test updates: 3 days (the ledger-kind change is small but touches two pinned test files — do it deliberately). P4 fog player_view + /theatre endpoint + facilitator spatial primitives: 2-3 days. P5 geo_sim interpolator + DTDL provenance mapping onto TheatreAsset: 3-4 days (client-heavy, engine-independent, can trail). Risk-weighted: P2's prompt tuning against real models is the schedule wildcard (+2-3 days if the cartographer over-moves or under-moves and the clamp table needs iteration); everything else is bounded because zero existing prompts, seeds, or goldens change.
risks: Async commit race with the facilitator seam: a deliver_inject spatial primitive between snapshot and commit is the one genuinely new concurrency surface; mitigated by theatre_version compare-and-set + per-line conflict drop, but the drop path itself needs a test or a stale cartographer line silently wins (the spatial silent-revert analog)

One-turn tripwire latency when the delta lands after the next briefing: a crossing the cartographer adjudicated can fire a boundary late; documented and bounded by the once-guard + staleness fence, but a facilitator watching the REFEREE layer will see truth move before the game reacts

LLM outage degrades the map to pure dead reckoning (router mock-substitute → 'NO SPATIAL CHANGES'): positions stay plausible but stop responding to narrative; only parse-health telemetry surfaces it, so a dashboard counter for SPATIAL_SIM fallbacks is needed or a whole campaign can run spatially deaf without anyone noticing

Spawned simulated entities are the fidelity feature AND the sprawl risk: caps (8 live, TTL 5) and the advisory-only tripwire rule contain adjudicative damage, but narrative references to expired entities can dangle — the fold/summary may mention a ship the TTL reaped

Kinematics clamp table is load-bearing truth: a wrong max_nm_per_turn silently converts every adjudicated move into a clamped 'estimated' crawl (or lets a frigate cross the Atlantic in a turn); needs scenario-review, not just code review

Fog noise is deterministic per (seed, entity, turn) — replay-stable, but that means a player who reloads sees identical estimates; acceptable, yet it makes the noise seed part of the de-facto save contract and it must never migrate to session rng draws

scores.name: TASKORD — Orders-Not-Positions Spatial Authority
scores.rationale: No raw coordinates ever leave the LLM: orders are set-membership-validated (unit registry, gazetteer, enums) with only a bounded bearing integer as numeric output. Kinematics is pure and RNG-free; degradation ladder bottoms out at doctrine dead-reckoning (stale-beats-false); fog noise uses a derived generator so child seeds are untouched; save story is the proven Optional-default idiom and old saves rehydrate to a live map. The appended round-3 call adds latency risk only marginally (parallel slot exists) but does shift master-RNG draws 2→3 — an honest, documented version fence. Slightly weaker than IRONCLAD on parse surface: 8 free-form pipe-delimited ORDER lines is a larger joint output than menu-echo selection, and 'zero wall-clock' for the third round-3 task is an overstatement if the movement call is the slowest of the three. Wrong-but-legal orders pass validation (shared weakness).

scores.name: IRONCLAD — Doctrine State Machine Spatial Layer
scores.rationale: Most robust by construction: movement never depends on the LLM at all — red plan phases advance from turn windows and metric bands (flags.py precedent), patrols are pure f(crc32(unit_id), turn), so a fully offline/mock campaign still produces a correct moving map. The LLM only echoes tokens from a menu the engine printed, the closest analog to the codebase's proven QUALITY/OUTCOME enum-echo pattern, with per-unit transition-graph validation catching illegal escalation jumps that TASKORD's flat enum check would pass. Fail-loud doctrine linter (turn-1 tripwire pre-fire check, unresolvable-location check) catches authoring errors at load, not mid-campaign. Same single-store/hidden-metrics-sync discipline, same save-compat idiom, same honest round-3 RNG version fence as TASKORD. Docked half a point for the same fence, the wrong-but-legal semantic gap it itself admits, and per-scenario doctrine.yaml being a recurring correctness surface (a mistyped route polyline is silent truth corruption until property tests catch it).

scores.name: CARTOGRAPHER: async world-simulator spatial layer
scores.rationale: Correctly keeps the briefing/adjudication request paths non-blocking and avoids master-RNG draws via a derived crc32 seed — genuinely clever. But it buys that with the codebase's first autonomous background mutation of world state: a new concurrency surface (snapshot/commit races with the facilitator seam, compare-and-set, per-line conflict drops, staleness fences) in a codebase built around a single threading.Lock and a destructive SSE queue — every one of those mechanisms is a new silent-revert trap needing its own test, and the design's own risk list enumerates three revert variants it must police forever. Worse for determinism than admitted: whether a delta commits before the next briefing is wall-clock/LLM-latency dependent, so tripwire firing turn and prompt contents vary run-to-run under identical seeds — replay and golden-transcript integrity are structurally broken while the design claims 'in-version determinism fully preserved.' The 'BRG/DISTnm from key' offset grammar plus SPAWN of novel entity ids is semi-raw geometric LLM output — exactly what the lens punishes — clamped after the fact rather than impossible by construction. A delta committing after a save (lost on reload) is unaddressed.

scores.name: TASKORD — Orders-Not-Positions Spatial Authority
scores.rationale: Best closed gameplay loop: the player's free-text intent becomes engine-enforced geometry (LLM emits orders, kinematics obeys), so 'send the carrier to the GIUK gap' is a real decision with ETAs, sensor coverage, and tripwire consequences. Fog is honest and playable — estimates grow with staleness and collapse under P-8/towed-array footprints, making ISR tasking a move with visible payoff. Every failure mode degrades to doctrine dead-reckoning, so the map moves and never lies even offline — the strongest 'stale beats false' story. The judge narrative is the cleanest of the three: 'the AI commands, physics adjudicates,' with a three-value provenance ladder that maps directly onto DTDL badges and an order_log that replays the campaign's actual geometry at AAR. Its realism (gazetteer, speed bands, kinematics) all surfaces as player-visible mechanics. Deductions: expressiveness capped at ~30 gazetteer ids plus coarse bearings (novel ambush geometry inexpressible), the red doctrine track can feel scripted once players learn it, and the 'zero wall-clock' claim for the third round-3 task is optimistic.

scores.name: IRONCLAD — Doctrine State Machine Spatial Layer
scores.rationale: Delivers the single best dread mechanic (a deterministic red clock the player watches close, with visible-in-advance tripwires) and the best fog-integrated eventing — visibility:'detected' tripwires that fire late and ambiguous when the picket is weak make detection posture retroactively matter. Readiness-as-live-state (surge-now-degraded vs wait-3-turns) and the 2-CAP QRA scarcity are genuinely tangible map decisions. But the gameplay ceiling is the hardest: every unmapped player intent is visibly refused, which reads as railroading exactly when a creative player is most engaged, and the LLM's spatial role shrinks to menu-echo — the weakest AI/DTDL narrative for judges ('the model picks from a printed list'). The doctrine pack is real recurring simulation/authoring burden whose payoff is legibility, not player agency, and the joint unit×posture×destination selection admits wrong-but-legal orders the validator cannot see. A superb wargame skeleton, a less alive game.

scores.name: CARTOGRAPHER: async world-simulator spatial layer
scores.rationale: Richest world texture — spawned color entities (a shadowing AGI, a P-8 line) make the map visibly react to the story, and the two-tier design guarantees motion under any failure. But through this lens the causal arrow is backwards: the cartographer moves units to match the already-written narrative, so geometry is a rendering of the story rather than a constraint the player plays against — positioning is less a decision than a consequence. The async seam costs honesty where it hurts most: tripwires can fire a turn late, the REFEREE layer sees truth move before the game reacts, and mid-turn delta commits mean advisors within one turn can see different worlds. The showcase feature (spawns) is deliberately advisory-only — fidelity without adjudicative payoff, which this lens punishes — and the LLM emitting quasi-positions (keys + BRG/DIST offsets) is the weakest 'map cannot lie' story of the three despite the clamp ladder. Excellent engineering hygiene (zero master-rng draws) that mostly doesn't cash out as gameplay.
