verified.claim: The 'projected computer screen in VR' workaround is sound: a CesiumJS canvas rendered flat and composited as a texture/layer inside a three.js (or Babylon) WebXR scene, so Cesium never touches the XR pipeline.
verified.evidence:
ARCHITECTURE = SOUND AND WELL-PRECEDENTED; naive version is NOT (render-loop and on-device-perf gotchas). Findings per sub-claim, raw:

(a) CANVAS-AS-TEXTURE MECHANICS — CONFIRMED. WebGL spec (registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/1.0): with preserveDrawingBuffer:false, using a WebGL canvas as texImage2D source AFTER the rendering task returns is undefined behavior (blank textures; same failure documented in gpuweb/gpuweb#4356). Two sound fixes: (1) Cesium `contextOptions:{webgl:{preserveDrawingBuffer:true}}` — the standard Cesium screenshot recipe (community.cesium.com/t/1781, /t/1380), small per-frame cost; (2) better: copy in the SAME JS task as the render — Cesium supports `useDefaultRenderLoop:false` + explicit `viewer.render()`; call it inside the XR rAF, then `gl.texImage2D(canvas)` immediately (also what `scene.postRender` capture exploits). Cross-context texture sharing is impossible (one context per canvas), so a copy is mandatory; in Chromium the canvas-source texImage2D path is GPU-accelerated (Chromium codereview 735623003 'WebGL: accelerated texImage2D/texSubImage2D for canvas'; chromium-dev thread: 'Chrome stores canvas content on the GPU already' — Firefox may fall back to CPU upload, bmo#1246410). Cost: 720p RGBA=3.7MB, 1080p=8.3MB per update; at 30Hz update / 72-90Hz XR ≈ 0.1-0.25GB/s GPU copy bandwidth — trivial on desktop, real-but-survivable on Quest. three.js CanvasTexture re-uploads the whole texture on needsUpdate=true; update at 24-30Hz, not per XR frame.

CRITICAL GOTCHA (breaks the naive design): during an immersive session on a standalone HMD, `window.requestAnimationFrame` is NOT guaranteed to fire (immersive-web/webxr#225; MDN XRSession.requestAnimationFrame: 'no guarantee the latter will work at all while an immersive XR session is underway'). Cesium's default render loop is window-rAF-driven, so it can silently freeze in-headset. The sound shape drives Cesium's render explicitly from `xrSession.requestAnimationFrame`.

(b) WEBXR LAYERS ON QUEST — CONFIRMED, QUEST-ONLY. Meta Quest/Oculus Browser ships full Layers (quad/cylinder/equirect/cube/media) enabled by default since Oculus Browser 16.1 (developers.meta.com blog); measured benefit in Meta's cube-layer sample: 2.4ms render-time saving, >25% total GPU load reduction; text/2D UI drawn to a layer is resampled ONCE by the compositor instead of twice → materially crisper text (Meta blog + immersive-web/layers explainer). Chrome (desktop/Android) supports ONLY XRProjectionLayer — no quad/cylinder/multi-layer (web-platform-dx/developer-signals#323; MDN XRQuadLayer = experimental, not Baseline). Sources for a quad layer: XRWebGLBinding = WebGL texture you copy the Cesium canvas into per update (no direct canvas binding exists — explainer confirms); XRMediaBinding = HTMLVideoElement only, zero-copy, compositor-driven ('displays the current frame of the video element with no additional interaction'). three.js merged mono quad+cylinder layer support with non-supporting-browser emulation (mrdoob/three.js PR #25254, by Layers spec editor Cabanier); Babylon has the WebXRLayers feature (doc.babylonjs.com WebXRLayers; forum threads incl. a real Quest 2 layers bug report — feature works but has rough edges). So: CanvasTexture-on-a-plane is the portable base; promote the panel to an XRQuadLayer on Quest for crisp text and cheaper composition.

(c) VIDEO-STREAMED VARIANT — CONFIRMED VIABLE, WITH ~quarter-second interaction latency. Measured WebRTC remote-rendering end-to-end latency (arxiv 2505.22132, laptop client): 1080p/15Mbps 289ms Wi-Fi / 270ms 5G; 720p 260/253ms; 480p 249/234ms; decode cost at 1080p ≈17% CPU / 5% GPU. Quest has hardware H.264 decode (WebRTC's safe codec); H.265/AV1-over-WebRTC on Quest Browser is an open question (Meta forum #1230235). Meta: media layers play video up to 8K@90fps on Quest 2 without dropped frames — a 1080p WebRTC stream into <video> → XRMediaBinding quad layer is near-zero page GPU cost and compositor-sharp. Verdict: ideal for a turn-based situation screen (FALSE FLAG's cadence); drag-to-rotate feels rubber-banded at ~250ms, so map continuous camera gestures client-side or accept it.

(d) CESIUMJS FLAT ON QUEST BROWSER — UNPROVEN, refusing to confirm. No public evidence of usable flat framerates found. Only concrete report: 'could not get the Sandcastle Cardboard demo to work properly on a Quest 2' (2021, community.cesium.com/t/14145); Cesium's own guidance for Quest was 'use Cesium for Unreal'. Quest Browser is Chromium-based so it will load, and Meta forum threads (e.g. BabylonJS-slow-FPS #1230168) show even single-engine 3D pages strain the SoC — Cesium's tile decode + two live GL contexts + stereo XR render is the risk stack. Requires a half-day on-device spike (globe at 720p, low-detail imagery, terrain off, `resolutionScale`<1, render every 2nd-3rd XR frame) before committing; otherwise use variant (c). Note the workaround's premise holds regardless: CesiumJS native WebXR (PR #11372) is still open, blit-based, AA-broken and explicitly unprioritized (maintainer ggetz, Oct 2024).

(e) INPUT RE-INJECTION — CONFIRMED, SHIPPING PATTERN. three.js addons do exactly this today: InteractiveGroup raycasts from the XR controller, takes `intersection.uv`, maps XR events {move→mousemove, select→click, selectstart/end→mousedown/up} and dispatches to the mesh; HTMLMesh converts uv→element coords (`clientX = x*element.offsetWidth + element.offsetLeft`) and dispatches real MouseEvent objects onto the DOM. Cesium's ScreenSpaceEventHandler consumes pointer/mouse events with client coords relative to canvas.getBoundingClientRect(), so synthetic PointerEvents work IF the hidden Cesium canvas keeps real layout dimensions (position it off-screen, not display:none, so its rect is non-degenerate). Caveats: wheel-zoom/pinch don't map from a ray — bind thumbstick/grip directly to Cesium's Camera API (camera.zoomIn/rotate) instead of faking wheel events; this is also more robust than emulating Cesium's drag inertia.

RECOMMENDED SHAPES (honest): [S1-portable] three.js plane + CanvasTexture; Cesium useDefaultRenderLoop:false, viewer.render() every Nth xrSession-rAF, same-task texImage2D copy (no preserveDrawingBuffer needed), InteractiveGroup/HTMLMesh-style synthetic pointers + Camera-API zoom. Works on desktop-tethered headsets at full quality today. [S2-Quest-quality] same, panel promoted to XRQuadLayer/XRCylinderLayer (three.js PR#25254 path or Babylon WebXRLayers); copy into layer texture only on change → compositor-sharp text, per-layer timewarp. [S3-Quest-safe] server-rendered Cesium → WebRTC H.264 1080p → <video> → XRMediaBinding quad layer; inputs via DataChannel to server-side synthetic events; ~250ms E2E, near-zero headset GPU. HARD LIMITS (inherent, all shapes): the globe is a monoscopic picture — no stereoscopic terrain, no parallax, no reaching 'into' the map (consistent with the prior 'decorative, never adjudicative' stance; the authoritative spatial layer lives in the engine, the screen just renders it); text legibility is poor via plain CanvasTexture unless texture res ≈2x apparent size or the layers path is used; comfort is fine (world-locked screen at 1-2m; latency on a screen ≠ head-motion latency).

Sources: https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/1.0/ ; https://github.com/gpuweb/gpuweb/discussions/4356 ; https://community.cesium.com/t/export-cesium-image-to-png-or-jpg-screenshot/1781 ; https://codereview.chromium.org/735623003 ; https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1246410 ; https://github.com/immersive-web/webxr/issues/225 ; https://developers.meta.com/horizon/blog/achieve-better-rendering-and-performance-with-webxr-layers-in-oculus-browser/ ; https://github.com/immersive-web/layers/blob/main/explainer.md ; https://github.com/web-platform-dx/developer-signals/issues/323 ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/XRQuadLayer ; https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/25254 ; https://doc.babylonjs.com/typedoc/classes/BABYLON.WebXRLayers ; https://arxiv.org/html/2505.22132v1 ; https://communityforums.atmeta.com/discussions/dev-other-dev/h265av1-hardware-decoding-support-for-webrtc-on-quest-3-using-browser-app/1230235 ; https://community.cesium.com/t/webxr-for-oculus-quest/14145 ; https://github.com/CesiumGS/cesium/pull/11372 ; https://community.cesium.com/t/webxr-in-cesiumjs/22948 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrdoob/three.js/dev/examples/jsm/interactive/InteractiveGroup.js ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrdoob/three.js/dev/examples/jsm/interactive/HTMLMesh.js ; https://communityforums.atmeta.com/discussions/dev-general/meta-quest-browser--babylonjs--slow-fps/1230168 ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/XRSession/requestAnimationFrame
conditions: Render-loop ownership: Cesium must be driven explicitly (useDefaultRenderLoop:false, viewer.render() inside xrSession.requestAnimationFrame) — window.requestAnimationFrame is not guaranteed to fire during an immersive session on standalone headsets, so the naive 'two parallel loops + copy' design silently freezes the globe on Quest.

Copy timing: texImage2D from the Cesium canvas must happen in the same JS task as Cesium's render, OR Cesium must be created with contextOptions.webgl.preserveDrawingBuffer:true; otherwise the WebGL spec makes the copy undefined behavior (blank texture). Textures cannot be shared across contexts — a per-update copy is unavoidable.
Update-rate discipline: cap CanvasTexture/layer updates at ~24-30Hz and 720p-1080p (3.7-8.3MB per upload); rely on Chromium's GPU-accelerated canvas-source texImage2D path (Firefox may CPU-fallback).

Quad/cylinder-layer benefits (single resampling → crisp text, ~2.4ms + >25% GPU savings per Meta's sample) exist ONLY on Meta Quest Browser (Oculus Browser ≥16.1); Chrome supports only XRProjectionLayer — ship the plain CanvasTexture plane as the portable base and promote to XRQuadLayer (three.js PR #25254 or Babylon WebXRLayers) when available.

On-device Quest feasibility (sub-claim d) is UNVERIFIED: no public evidence of CesiumJS running flat in Quest Browser at usable framerates (only a 2021 failure report); commit to it only after an on-device spike with degraded settings (720p, terrain off, resolutionScale<1, render every 2nd-3rd frame) — otherwise use the server-rendered WebRTC variant.

Video-streamed variant carries ~235-290ms measured end-to-end latency (fine for a turn-based situation screen, rubber-bandy for drag-to-rotate) and should target H.264 into an XRMediaBinding quad layer on Quest; H.265/AV1-over-WebRTC support on Quest Browser is unconfirmed.

Input re-injection is a shipping pattern (three.js InteractiveGroup + HTMLMesh: controller ray → intersection.uv → synthetic MouseEvent with client coords) but the hidden Cesium canvas must keep a real layout rect (off-screen positioning, not display:none), and zoom/pinch should bypass event synthesis and drive Cesium's Camera API from controller axes.

Accepted inherent limits: the globe is a monoscopic 'screen' — no stereoscopic terrain or parallax (consistent with the prior 'decorative, never adjudicative' ruling); text is legible only via the layers path or ~2x-resolution textures; comfort is fine because the panel is world-locked and screen-content latency is not head-motion latency.

ideas.title: Spatial verbs the interpreter honors
ideas.description: Free-text like 'move the carrier group to the GIUK gap and put a Type-23 picket off Faslane' produces actual engine movement, not flavor prose. The closed Mission enum (hold/transit/patrol/screen/shadow/intercept/strike/rtb) gives the player a spatial verb set the game guarantees to execute, and the interpretation phase pre-nominates which hulls the player meant so the movement order lands on the right unit.
ideas.mechanism: The decision-interpretation prompt already requests a FORCES INVOLVED line (data/prompts/decision_interpretation.txt:29) that the engine throws away — parsed only for CLI display at cli/display_utils.py:194, and the LLM-context audit (audits/2026-08-05-llm-context/SCHEMATIC.md:432) confirms nothing validates or consumes it. Parse that free, already-paid-for label against the unit registry (exact-match, never fuzzy) to pre-highlight tasked units in TASKORD's round-3 MOVEMENT call (appended to decision_phase.py:492-505's round 3, which has a free worker slot at MAX_ROUND_WORKERS=3, decision_phase.py:91). Orders are set-membership validated (unit registry, gazetteer, enums) so the verb either executes exactly or is visibly refused with the sim_loop.py:288 'Skipped:' transcript template — never silently reinterpreted.
ideas.payoff: The core promise of the whole spatial layer, delivered at the player's fingertips: positioning becomes a real decision with ETAs, coverage and tripwire consequences, and the wrong-but-legal unit-selection risk (both judges flagged it) is cut by wiring the player's own named forces into the order menu — signal the game already asks for and discards every turn.

ideas.title: Pre-commit geometry preview with live range rings
ideas.description: During the interpret → preview → confirm gate, the player sees the projected turn before committing: where every unit will be, arrival snaps, and — critically — whether weapon envelopes will intersect. 'Can 96 Sea Viper rounds matter from where the Type-45s actually are' and 'are we inside Tomahawk range of anything' become questions answered by rings on the globe during deliberation, not after adjudication.
ideas.mechanism: run_preview_round (engine/decision_phase.py:236-273) is the sanctioned preview seam with the ER-074 pay-once contract; because engine/kinematics.advance() is pure and RNG-free, it can dry-run on a deep-copied SpatialState with the provisional orders at preview time with zero determinism cost and zero double-advance risk (movement is commit-only). Range rings are computed by intersecting launcher UnitTrack positions with the exact stockpile counts get_resources already serves from initial_conditions.yaml (96 Sea Viper, 30 Tomahawk; StockpileItem at api/server.py:369). The projection is emitted with provenance='projected' on the /theatre-style state endpoint and never persisted — a view, not state, per the single-store rule.
ideas.payoff: Converts the discussion phase into a maneuver-planning session — the exact window where pushback and omissions already fire — and makes stockpiles intersect with geography for the first time: 'can we even engage from here' becomes adjudicable and visible before the player spends the turn.

ideas.title: Advisors and the omissions scan quote real geometry
ideas.description: CDS says 'at 16 knots they are 18 hours from our territorial waters' and it is arithmetic, not vibes. The pre-adjudication critical-omissions scan flags computed coverage gaps — 'no P-8 coverage of the gap', 'both Type-45s are south while the threat axis is north' — detected by the engine, narrated by the LLM.
ideas.mechanism: A deterministic derived-facts appendix (closing speed from speed-band tables, ETA hours, CPA, per-sensor coverage gaps) is computed by kinematics helpers and appended to the SPATIAL PICTURE block in the fast-moving tail of build_shared_context_prefix (context_builder.py:378-395; test_prompt_cache_order.py-safe position), so ADVISOR_PUSHBACK (agents/conversation.py:390) and ADVISOR_QA (:219) ground their lines in engine numbers. check_critical_omissions (agents/conversation.py:455; pre-adjudication hook per docs/CRITICAL_OMISSIONS_SYSTEM.md:13) receives engine-detected spatial-omission candidates as facts-to-consider — the LLM chooses which to voice, but cannot invent geometry, because the candidates are the only spatial claims in its context.
ideas.payoff: The cheapest credibility multiplier in the design: every advisor line that cites a real ETA teaches the player the map is truth, and the omissions system — currently judgment-only — gains a class of provably correct warnings that make ignoring geography feel like ignoring a staff officer with a ruler.

ideas.title: Tripwire beats replace the scripted timeline
ideas.description: Campaign pacing derives from actual closure geometry instead of authored turn numbers. The GIUK crossing, the 200nm-from-Faslane threshold, the Kalibr-envelope-of-London ring fire when the fleet actually gets there — so shadowing, delaying, or facilitator-rerouting red genuinely re-paces every downstream beat. A fleet can no longer cross the GIUK gap during a turn the game calls quiet.
ideas.mechanism: Declarative predicates (zone_entry/closing_within/range_ring/eta_below) evaluated at the one provably quiescent instant — top of GameManager.get_turn_briefing (engine/game_manager.py:182) — delivered through the full deliver_inject primitive set including the hidden-metrics sync (game_manager.py:296-307, dodging the silent-revert trap). On scripted-exhausted turns the firing tripwire BECOMES the turn's inject where sim_loop.py:379-399 currently falls back to 'no significant developments' (the IRONCLAD quiet-turn graft). PlayedEvent.kind='system' admits crossings durably into EVENTS ALREADY PLAYED without absorbing the player's turn verdict (record_played_event overwrite keyed same-turn+same-kind), closing the issue-#25 restage class for geometric events.
ideas.payoff: Escalation acquires spatial teeth with deterministic timing: the player can read the threat clock off the globe and race it, and the scenario author stops hand-scheduling beats that the map might contradict — emergent injects with authored consequences, the best of both.

ideas.title: Trail-or-lose: shadowing and intercept as pursuit kinematics
ideas.description: 'shadow' keeps an SSN in trail behind a red group and — the payoff — holds the contact solid: the fog error radius collapses to zero while trail is maintained. 'intercept' computes a real great-circle intercept point against the target's standing-order track. Red reacts: a detected shadow can trigger a doctrine-graph flank sprint that breaks trail if blue can't match speed, and the player watches the uncertainty ellipse bloom.
ideas.mechanism: Both missions resolve inside the pure kinematics module against the target's standing MovementOrder — no LLM, no RNG. Shadow refreshes UnitTrack.last_confirmed_turn every turn trail holds, which engine/intel_picture.py's staleness function reads directly (error radius grows with turns-since-confirmed, collapses in sensor footprint). Red's reaction rides the already-designed REFEREE-only tripwire channel ('blue carrier zone_entry GIUK_gap feeds red doctrine reaction', filtered from player streams at server.py:823-831) driving a legal transition in IRONCLAD's per-unit doctrine graph — red cannot jump phases, only sprint within its plan, so the counterplay is bounded and learnable.
ideas.payoff: A genuine deterministic ASW mini-game inside the narrative wargame: maintain-trail vs re-task is a turn-by-turn dilemma with rendered consequence, and it is the mechanic that makes the 15-boat red fleet feel like a hunt rather than a countdown.

ideas.title: Spatial ending predicates
ideas.description: Win and loss conditions the globe can render: 'resolution requires red withdrawn north of the GIUK line'; 'the decapitation-strike ending is reachable only while red holds inside the Kalibr envelope of London'. The ending prose can no longer assert geography the authoritative map contradicts — the verdict IS geometry the player steered.
ideas.mechanism: check_ending (engine/endings.py:113, invoked only in resolve_decision pre-advance; final_turn grading at :135) gains opt-in pure-geometry predicates over SpatialState. The ordering already works with zero added latency: kinematics.advance runs after pipeline sync (game_manager.py:566-574) and before check_ending/turn++ (:586-593), so endings grade post-movement state the same turn — unlike tripwire-metric endings, which accept the documented one-turn deferral. Shipped as the explicit versioned opt-in the prior study deferred, honoring classic mode's on-screen promise of 'clear thresholds and win' conditions (endings.py:3).
ideas.payoff: Closes the last honesty gap (ending text vs map) and gives the campaign a spatial victory the player can literally watch approach — withdrawal north across a line on the globe is an ending condition, a narrative image, and a rendered animation all at once.

ideas.title: ISR tasking with a rendered receipt: fog you spend to shrink
ideas.description: Tasking the P-8s up, pushing a towed-array frigate forward, or keeping an SSN in trail visibly shrinks red uncertainty ellipses the next turn; re-tasking them visibly grows them. The YAML's CRITICAL LIMITATION — 2 simultaneous CAPs for the entire UK — becomes literal coverage circles, so choosing what to leave unwatched is a map decision with a visible hole in it.
ideas.mechanism: engine/intel_picture.py: sensor footprints (P-8 North Atlantic ring when on-station, Type-23 towed-array radius, SSN trail) collapse the estimate offset; staleness grows it via the derived generator Random(hash((seed,unit_id,turn,'fog'))) — replay-stable and never touching self.rng, so the decision_phase.py:166 child-seed sequence and resumed saves are untouched. engine/intelligence.py:196-199's fabricated rng.randint(150,250)nm ranges are rewired to quote the same estimate layer, so INTEL prose, the resources panel (get_resources live-merge, game_manager.py:1018-1129), and the globe agree for the first time. Player /geo/stream and view=player renders estimate+radius; facilitator view renders truth with the estimate overlaid.
ideas.payoff: ISR becomes a move with visible payoff — the mechanic that makes a deception-centred scenario playable as a deception game: EXCON's truth-vs-estimate gap is the false flag, rendered, and the player's sensor allocation is how they fight it.

ideas.title: The ops-room table where the dread clock is drawn
ideas.description: The COBRA war-room diorama and multi-screen ops room become where geometry is FELT: because red doctrine legs and speed bands are deterministic standing orders, the client projects them forward and literally draws the countdown — 'GIUK crossing in ~2 turns at present speed' as an arc creeping across the table — with the 200nm-Faslane and Kalibr-London tripwire rings drawn in advance so the room watches the crossing approach. headline: The supplement's biggest holes are the prior study's four still-valid operational findings that no reader, design, judge, or idea touched: zero-auth security (which now guards ground truth, facilitator teleports, and a network-reachable movement prompt), accessibility (now including in-headset shader photosensitivity), the pace_s<=30 mock cap plus the never-measured real-LLM turn time, and session-lifecycle leaks that the new per-session daemons/queues worsen — all four must be carried forward and re-scoped for the truth layer.

The judging is unresolved: a 1-1 winner split (IRONCLAD 9.0 vs TASKORD 8.5) that the ideas material papers over by crowning TASKORD — the supplement must present the tiebreak or ship the hybrid both judges' grafts converge on (TASKORD emission + kinematics, IRONCLAD transition graphs / detected-visibility tripwires / readiness state, derived-seed movement call).

I verified the one load-bearing unverified claim in-repo: tripwire lines written at the top of get_turn_briefing DO land inside the inject generator's LAST TURN slice (get_last_turn_slice at llm/context_builder.py:161-204 slices from the previous TURN header; the new header is written after the hook; head-trimming preserves the newest lines) — upgrade to confirmed, fix the wrong prompts.py citation, pin with a test.

Save discipline is executably verified but the plans are incomplete: every design omits the docs/game.zip play-bundle rebuild (4 tests fail on any models/world.py edit until dev-scripts/build_play_bundle.py runs) and none states the Pyodide browser-play surface's spatial behavior; add both, and present new-save-in-old-code silent loss as an explicit accepted-loss owner decision.

The decorative MVP remains the right commitment gate but its scripted red-fleet tracks should be cut — the ~1-week zero-LLM truth-map stage supersedes them; the supplement must give one sequencing recommendation, revoke 'engine-untouched' explicitly, and state a combined solo-dev estimate (~2-3 months part-time) against a competition deadline that is still unpinned.

The VR answer is sound only in conditioned form: Cesium driven from xrSession.requestAnimationFrame with a same-task canvas copy, layer benefits Quest-only, Quest-flat Cesium performance unproven pending an on-device spike (and a Quest whose existence is still unconfirmed) — and it extends, not reverses, the prior 'no CesiumJS in the XR pipeline' ruling.
